evidence_tags.evidence: Evidence-based: the number or shape comes from a cited peer-reviewed study or meta-analysis.
evidence_tags.extrapolated: Extrapolated: pooled or neighbouring evidence stretched to a muscle, level or range the studies did not measure directly.
evidence_tags.modeled: Modeled: a planning convention chosen by Coach. Not measured; adjust to how you actually respond.

schoenfeld2017.cite: Schoenfeld, Ogborn & Krieger (2017). Dose-response relationship between weekly resistance training volume and increases in muscle mass: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Journal of Sports Sciences 35(11):1073-1082.
schoenfeld2017.used_for: 15 studies / 34 groups. Mean gains 5.4% (<5 weekly sets, ES 0.307), 6.6% (5-9, ES 0.378), 9.8% (10+, ES 0.520); 3-level trend P = 0.074; continuous model +0.37% per weekly set (P = 0.002). vol8g: 5.4/9.8 ~ 55% is the nearest evidence for the minimum anchor (vol12: 60%, rule of thumb). Published online 2016, issue 2017.

pelland2025.cite: Pelland et al. The Resistance Training Dose Response: Meta-Regressions Exploring the Effects of Weekly Volume and Frequency on Muscle Hypertrophy and Strength Gains. Sports Medicine 56(2):481-505 (2026 issue; online Dec 2025). Earlier version: SportRxiv preprint 2024 (not peer-reviewed), doi 10.51224/srxiv.460.
pelland2025.used_for: 67 studies. Counting indirect sets as 0.5 ("fractional") fit best. Hypertrophy keeps rising with weekly volume with diminishing returns; best-fit hypertrophy model was a square-root curve. Basis for the square-root curve shape and for keeping ~0.5 credit on indirect sets. vol8g: diminishing returns basis for the sweet-spot and D anchors and a plateau below 100% (preprint 2024 and Sports Med 2025 cited separately, preprint labelled).
pelland2025.cite_history_vol12: Pelland et al. The Resistance Training Dose Response: Meta-Regressions Exploring the Effects of Weekly Volume and Frequency on Muscle Hypertrophy and Strength Gains. Sports Medicine (online Dec 2025). Earlier version: SportRxiv preprint 2024 (not peer-reviewed), doi 10.51224/srxiv.460.

bazvalle2022.cite: Baz-Valle, Balsalobre-Fernandez, Alix-Fages & Santos-Concejero (2022). A Systematic Review of the Effects of Different Resistance Training Volumes on Muscle Hypertrophy. Journal of Human Kinetics 81:199-210.
bazvalle2022.used_for: Trained young men: 12-20 weekly sets per muscle a reasonable range; >20 no clear extra gain for quads and biceps (triceps an exception, with pressing counted). Basis for 12-18/20 sweet spots and the ~20 diminishing-returns point on big muscles.

robinson2024.cite: Robinson, Pelland, Remmert, Refalo, Jukic, Steele & Zourdos (2024). Exploring the Dose-Response Relationship Between Estimated Resistance Training Proximity to Failure, Strength Gain, and Muscle Hypertrophy: A Series of Meta-Regressions. Sports Medicine 54(9):2209-2231.
robinson2024.used_for: Hypertrophy increases as sets end closer to failure (negative slope per estimated RIR); exploratory, RIR estimated, exact shape unclear. Basis for discounting sets with more reps in reserve; the specific multipliers are extrapolated/modeled.

refalo2023.cite: Refalo, Helms, Trexler, Hamilton & Fyfe (2023). Influence of Resistance Training Proximity-to-Failure on Skeletal Muscle Hypertrophy: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis. Sports Medicine 53(3):649-665.
refalo2023.used_for: Failure vs non-failure gave similar hypertrophy when volume was equated. Supports full credit at 0-2 RIR (no bonus for failure).

refalo2024.cite: Refalo, Helms, Robinson, Hamilton & Fyfe (2024). Similar muscle hypertrophy following eight weeks of resistance training to momentary muscular failure or with repetitions-in-reserve in resistance-trained individuals. Journal of Sports Sciences 42(1):85-101.
refalo2024.used_for: Quads: failure vs 1-2 RIR gave the same growth; failure caused more acute fatigue. Supports multiplier 1.0 through RIR 2 and a failure surcharge on recovery, not on stimulus.

moran2017.cite: Moran-Navarro et al. (2017). Time course of recovery following resistance training leading or not to failure. European Journal of Applied Physiology.
moran2017.used_for: Trained men, bench and squat: non-failure protocols recovered mechanical performance faster between 24 and 48 h; failure slowed recovery by up to 24-48 h, some markers still off at 72 h. Anchors the 24-72 h range and the failure factor.

cheung2003.cite: Cheung, Hume & Maxwell (2003). Delayed onset muscle soreness: treatment strategies and performance factors. Sports Medicine 33(2):145-164.
cheung2003.used_for: Soreness after unaccustomed, eccentric-heavy work rises within 24 h and peaks around 24-72 h. Basis for the stretch/eccentric factor and the 96 h clamp.

mchugh2003.cite: McHugh (2003). Recent advances in the understanding of the repeated bout effect. Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports 13(2):88-97.
mchugh2003.used_for: Repeated exposure protects against damage from the same work. Basis for the beginner recovery factor (less protection on novel work); the 1.15 value is modeled.

schoenfeld2016rest.cite: Schoenfeld, Pope, Benik et al. (2016). Longer Interset Rest Periods Enhance Muscle Strength and Hypertrophy in Resistance-Trained Men. Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research 30(7):1805-1812.
schoenfeld2016rest.used_for: 3 min beat 1 min rest on compound lifts for trained men. Supports ~3 min rest for primary lifts at intermediate/advanced.

singer2024rest.cite: Singer, Wolf, Generoso et al. (2024). Give it a rest: a systematic review with Bayesian meta-analysis on the effect of inter-set rest interval duration on muscle hypertrophy. Frontiers in Sports and Active Living 6:1429789.
singer2024rest.used_for: Small advantage for resting >60 s; no clear extra hypertrophy benefit beyond ~90 s. Supports 1.5 min isolation rest at every level.

rp_landmarks.cite: Renaissance Periodization: Israetel, Hoffmann & Smith, Scientific Principles of Hypertrophy Training (2021) and RP "training volume landmarks" articles (MV/MEV/MAV/MRV).
rp_landmarks.used_for: PRACTITIONER, NOT PEER-REVIEWED. The three-zone idea (minimum effective, adaptive sweet spot, recoverable maximum) and the low direct minimum for front delts and traps given pressing/pulling. Used for zone structure and small-muscle sweet spots only; no RP number is copied as evidence. Note RP counts direct sets only; our zones are in fractional effective sets.

remmert2025session.cite: Remmert, Pelland, Robinson, Hinson & Zourdos (2025). Is There Too Much of a Good Thing? Meta-Regressions of the Effect of Per-Session Volume on Hypertrophy and Strength. SportRxiv PREPRINT (not peer-reviewed); conference abstract (not a full paper): Joachim, Remmert, Pelland, Robinson, Hinson & Zourdos, Medicine & Science in Sports & Exercise 58(10S), 2026, doi 10.1249/01.mss.0001259712.79343.1b (same ~11 fractional sets PUOS). No full peer-reviewed version found as of 2026-11-01.
remmert2025session.used_for: PREPRINT. Hypertrophy rises with per-session volume with diminishing returns from the start; best-fit hypertrophy model linear-log; point of undetectable outcome superiority ~11 fractional sets per session (more sets still added a little, with a much smaller slope and wide uncertainty; too little data at very high per-session volumes). Reports an unpublished analysis by Krieger finding diminishing returns above 6-8 total sets per session with >= 2 min rest (not verified by us; unpublished). Basis for the per-session knee near 8-12 sets for a large muscle.

schoenfeld2019freq.cite: Schoenfeld, Grgic & Krieger (2019). How many times per week should a muscle be trained to maximize muscle hypertrophy? A systematic review and meta-analysis of studies examining the effects of resistance training frequency. Journal of Sports Sciences 37(11):1286-1295.
schoenfeld2019freq.used_for: vol8d: 25 studies; no significant hypertrophy difference between higher and lower frequency when weekly volume is equated. Basis for keeping the one-session vs two-session gap small (~5-7% on the weekly %).

macdougall1995.cite: MacDougall, Gibala, Tarnopolsky, MacDonald, Interisano & Yarasheski (1995). The time course for elevated muscle protein synthesis following heavy resistance exercise. Canadian Journal of Applied Physiology 20(4):480-486.
macdougall1995.used_for: In trained young men, biceps muscle protein synthesis was ~50% higher at 4 h and ~109% higher at 24 h after 12 sets to failure, and back to within ~14% of the control arm (not significant) by ~36 h. Basis for "the growth signal from one session lasts roughly 1-2 days in trained lifters".

damas2016.cite: Damas, Phillips, Libardi, Vechin, Lixandrao, Jannig, et al. (2016). Resistance training-induced changes in integrated myofibrillar protein synthesis are related to hypertrophy only after attenuation of muscle damage. Journal of Physiology 594(18):5209-5222.
damas2016.used_for: Measured integrated myofibrillar protein synthesis over 0-48 h after a session at weeks 1, 3 and 10 of training; once damage had subsided (weeks 3 and 10) the 0-48 h response correlated with hypertrophy (r ~0.9). Supports a 48 h window as the relevant post-session period in trained muscle.

schoenfeld2016freq.cite: Schoenfeld, Ogborn & Krieger (2016). Effects of resistance training frequency on measures of muscle hypertrophy: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Sports Medicine 46(11):1689-1697.
schoenfeld2016freq.used_for: Training a muscle twice a week gave larger hypertrophy effect sizes than once a week (0.49 vs 0.30; 10 studies). The later, larger volume-equated analysis (Schoenfeld 2019) found frequency mattered little when weekly sets are equal, so "too long a gap" is an info note, not a warning.

zones.unit: weekly effective sets (after credit rules and the per-session discount)

definition.min: Minimum: where the model's growth zone starts (= targets.json min x levelMinFactor; same blue/green edge as today). Sets below it still count.
definition.sweet_lo..sweet_hi: Sweet spot: the range the model favours for this muscle and level.
definition.diminishing: Diminishing-returns point (= targets.json max; amber starts above it, same as rules.json volume_bands). Past it, extra sets add little modeled stimulus for their recovery cost.

level_rule.sweet: intermediate sweet spot x {"beginner": [0.75, 0.85], "intermediate": [1.0, 1.0], "advanced": [1.0, 1.0]} (lo, hi), kept above min+1 and at least 2 wide

chest.note: Large muscle; studied mostly through bench-type pressing in pooled data.

front_delts.note: Gets most of its work from pressing (credited at the discounted secondary rate). Direct front-delt work is rarely needed once pressing is in the plan.

traps.note: Gets indirect work from rows, deadlifts and shrug-like pulls.

triceps.note: Baz-Valle 2022 found >20 sets helped triceps when pressing was counted; the model keeps 18 as the point where returns flatten.

curve.replaces: targets.json curve (S = 1 - exp(-x/k), k = level min / ln 2.5)
curve.formula: Per muscle m with intermediate edges (min, sweet_lo, sweet_hi, D) and anchors (60%, 76%, 86%, 89%): (vol8i: per level, params_by_level[user level]; anchors_pct[0] can exceed 0.6 where a concave fallback applied) 0 < x <= min: S = a_min ln(1 + x/k) / ln(1 + min/k) (k = log_k); min < x <= D: quadratic pieces S = za + sa (x - xa) + curv (x - xa)^2 from pieces [xa, xb, za, sa, curv]; x > D: S = 0.89 + (plateau - 0.89)(1 - exp(-(x - D)/tau)), plateau = 0.979. Input x = the capped weekly value min(x_equiv, raw).

params.interpolation:
(smooth C1, monotone, concave; a model, not a measurement):
- 0..min: log segment S = a1 * ln(1 + x/k) / ln(1 + min/k), k solved so its end slope equals the knot slope at min (steep start, like vol5).
- min..D: Schumaker shape-preserving quadratic spline (Schumaker 1983) through the anchors; knot slopes = harmonic mean of the adjacent
  secants (min, sweet_lo, sweet_hi); slope at D = 2*secant_last - slope(sweet_hi), so the last interval is one quadratic.
- past D: S = a4 + (P - a4)(1 - exp(-(x - D)/tau)), plateau P = 1.1 * a4 (97.9%, below 100%), tau = (P - a4)/S'(D) (slope-continuous).

curve.reads_as: share of this muscle's modeled plateau. Every muscle reads 60% at its minimum (advanced exceptions: see concave_fallback), 76% at sweet-spot low, 86% at sweet-spot high, 89% at its diminishing point, approaching 97.9% beyond. Compare % within one muscle; the zone label carries the cross-muscle meaning.

tags.shape: modeled (anchored per muscle; concave diminishing returns per Pelland 2024 PREPRINT / 2025)
tags.min_anchor: rule of thumb (vol12: 60%; Schoenfeld 2017 low/high-volume gain ratio ~55% is the nearest evidence)
tags.plateau_beyond_D: modeled (Baz-Valle 2022: no clear extra gain >20 sets for quads/biceps)

per_set.formula: per set n: 1/(1 + (n-1)/c); workout stimulus = sum over its effective sets (fractional last set pro rata); c per anchor group (vol8h, session.per_muscle[m].c; vol8d was 1.0 x heavy anchor, vol8 0.4 x)

smooth_vol5.formula: s <= a: g = s; s > a: g = a + b ln(1 + (s - a)/b); a = 0.8 x H, b = 0.4 x H, H = targets.json session.muscles[m].heavy

session_discount.legacy: cap/factor = the pre-vol5 hard cut (10 sets, then 50%); kept only so an unported client still runs.
session_discount.tag: modeled (smooth log shape; vol8h c per anchor group calibrated so one workout is 4-10% below 2 days on the vol8g weekly %, per Schoenfeld 2019 / Pelland 2025)
session_discount.note: vol9: no session discount on weekly volume. per_set kept for the session_efficiency display only.

curve.fit_vs_evidence: Pelland et al. (Sports Medicine 2025) compared 7 functional forms for fractional weekly sets vs hypertrophy (linear, spline, linear-log, polynomial, square root, quadratic, reciprocal) with a BIC-approximated Bayes factor and picked square root as the best fit; the paper does not print the margin over linear-log in the main text, so we cannot say how close the log fit was, and the authors state the data remain compatible with multiple functional forms, with few studies above ~25 weekly sets. Their efficiency tiers (minimum effective dose 4 sets; 5-10 higher, 11-18 intermediate, 19-29 lower efficiency) describe per-set efficiency, not a share of a ceiling. Scaled so both read 91% at 20 sets, Pelland's square-root point estimate puts 8 sets at ~58% and 12-18 at ~70-86%; the active log curve puts 8 at 70% and 12-18 at ~79-89%, i.e. it front-loads low volumes more than Pelland's point estimate. That is a coaching choice (Mr Dude's anchors), not a better fit. The per-session preprint (Remmert 2025) did find linear-log best for per-session volume. No study measures "% of plateau", so the percentages are a display convention.

input.weekly_value: sum over the week of effective sets (rating x proximity; secondary and minor roles), no per-set decay, no x_equiv mapping, no cap
input.weekly_pct: curve per_muscle[m].params_by_level[user level] at weekly_value (vol8i anchors unchanged)
input.zones_and_colours: weekly_value rounded to 0.01 against the level zones (unchanged).
input.superseded: vol8b x_equiv (even-2x inverse mapping) and the vol8c min(x_equiv, raw) cap: kept under input_vol8 for history.

vol5_log.formula: c = D/45; x <= D: S = ln(1 + x/c) / ln(1 + D/c) / 1.1  (= 0.909 at D);  x > D: S = (1 + 0.1*(1 - exp(-(x-D)/tau))) / 1.1, tau = 0.1 * (c + D) * ln(1 + D/c) (slope-continuous);  D = zones diminishing point (targets.max)

anchors_rule.why_86_89: Requested ~85% at sweet_hi and ~90% at D. For the 10 muscles whose D is only 2 sets past sweet_hi (chest, lats, upper back, quads, biceps, triceps, calves, hamstrings, glutes, lower back) 85 -> 90 over 2 sets is steeper per set than 76 -> 85 over the 4-6 sets before, which breaks diminishing returns (concavity). 86% / 89% is the closest uniform pair (1 point each) that stays concave for every muscle.
anchors_rule.levels: vol8i: anchors per level. Each level's curve passes through that level's own zone edges with the same percentages (60/76/86/89), and the % uses the user's level (e.g. beginner chest 6/9/15.5/20 sets, advanced chest 10/12/18/20). Where a level's minimum sits only 2 sets below sweet-low (advanced chest/lats/upper back/quads 10 vs 12, advanced biceps/triceps/hamstrings/glutes 8 vs 10), 60% at the minimum is not concave, so the minimum anchor is raised just enough (nearest concave fit; see concave_fallback). The per-set decay c is also per level (rules.json session_dose.c_by_level). Colours and warnings use each level's own zones as before.
anchors_rule.source_of_truth: volume-model.json curve.per_muscle[m].anchors_by_level[level] (targets.json curve.anchors now only points here)

min_vol12.label: rule of thumb
min_vol12.note: Rule of thumb, not a measured value. The nearest evidence (Schoenfeld, Ogborn & Krieger 2017: <5 vs 10+ weekly sets, 5.4% vs 9.8% mean gain ~ 55%) puts the low-volume end at a bit over half; 60% is a round planning number slightly above it.

curve.basis: Anchors are modeled, calibrated to the evidence below, not measured per muscle. Minimum 60% (vol12: rule of thumb; nearest evidence): Schoenfeld, Ogborn & Krieger 2017 (J Sports Sci 35(11):1073-82; 15 studies, 34 groups) found mean gains of 5.4% (<5 weekly sets, ES 0.307), 6.6% (5-9, ES 0.378) and 9.8% (10+, ES 0.520); 5.4/9.8 = 55%, so the low-volume end delivers a bit over half of a solid dose (the 3-level comparison was a trend, P = 0.074; the continuous model was significant, +0.37% per weekly set). Sweet spot 76-86% and D 89% with a plateau below 100%: Pelland et al. (SportRxiv PREPRINT 2024, doi 10.51224/srxiv.460; peer-reviewed Sports Med 2025, doi 10.1007/s40279-025-02344-w) found hypertrophy keeps rising with weekly volume with diminishing returns (no clear plateau inside the studied range). The exact percentages are planning choices.

input_vol8.x_dec: sum over the week's workouts of the per-set-decayed workout stimulus (session.credit)
input_vol8.x_equiv: the raw weekly sets x such that 2 x g(x/2) = x_dec (g = session.credit for that muscle); solve by bisection (monotone)
input_vol8.weekly_pct: curve.formula(x_equiv, D) with D = zones diminishing
input_vol8.why: Mapping the decayed total back to its 2-sessions-a-week raw equivalent means an even 2x split reads exactly its raw sets on the curve (so the anchors hold at the zone edges for that layout); one heavy session reads lower, 3 light sessions are capped at raw. vol8g: the curve is the per-muscle anchored curve (Mr Dude withdrew the earlier chest 70%-at-8 pick as speculation).
input_vol8.zones_and_colours: vol8c: the weekly value = min(x_equiv, raw weekly effective sets) drives the %, the colours and the warnings against the existing zones (x_equiv is already in 2x/week raw-set units, so the zones need no recalibration). The cap stops 3+ light days inflating the total. Compare at the boundaries after rounding to 0.01 (checker does; the app must do the same).

credit.formula: effective(set, muscle) = rating x prox(RIR_set + offset[role]); rating < 0.25 -> 0; then per-session discount

prime.rule: muscle with the exercise's highest rating (ties all prime), or rating >= 0.75

credit.rir_offset_tag: modeled (a synergist that is not the limiting muscle is further from its own failure; no study measures the offset)

planned_rir_default.note: Planner tiles carry no RIR: use these (logging-spec target RIR 1-3, isolation 0-2). Prime movers therefore score exactly as today in the planner.

credit.logged: Use set.rir (0-4, 4 = 4+). Null RIR = planned default for that exercise type (logging-spec: no RIR logged still counts).
credit.vs_current: Current: every set adds sets x rating (>= 0.25) whatever the RIR. New: prime movers unchanged at RIR 0-2; secondary movers at planned RIR get x0.9, minor movers x0.8; logged sets at RIR 3/4 lose 10%/20% (more for synergists).
credit.warnings_rounding: none (vol6): zones, colours and warnings use exact effective sets; 0.5 rounding is display-only (targets.json counting.display_round_to)
credit.tag: rating from exercises.json (modeled coaching estimates, 0.5 ~ Pelland fractional); prox 0-2 evidence, 3-4 extrapolated, 5+ modeled

recovery.recommendation: Show both: estimated recovery hours per muscle per session (for spacing) and the week against generic benchmark routines (for total load). Drop raw "pts" from the UI; keep % of saved baseline as an optional third line.
recovery.hours_formula: vol11b: see recovery.load_vol11b.formula (exact steps). 1. Per tile and muscle m: c = sets x rating x prox[RIR] (credit; 0 if rating < 0.25), f = sets x rating x fatigue_per_set x effort[RIR] (muscle fatigue). Use full floats. 2. ES = sum c, ST = sum c over tiles whose exercise is in stretch_biased[m], F = sum f. 3. Round half-up to 0.01: r2(x) = floor(x x 100 + 0.5 + 1e-9) / 100. ES2 = r2(ES), F2 = r2(F), share = r2(ST / ES). 4. Gate: if ES2 < 1.00 then hours = 0 (no bar, no recovery days). assumptions: Hours are for the muscle to be ready to train hard again, not for soreness to vanish.
They assume normal sleep, eating and stress; those change real recovery and are not modeled.
Newer lifters get a 15% longer estimate; intermediate and advanced use the same baseline.
Recovery adds up set by set: each effective set beyond 2 adds about 4 hours, more if it is close to failure (RIR 0: x1.2, RIR 1: x1.1) and less if it is easy (RIR 3: x0.9, RIR 4+: x0.8).

Heavy spine-loading lifts (squats, deadlifts, good mornings) count 1.3x per set, other free-weight compounds 1.1x, machine and cable compounds 1.0x, isolation 0.9x. These weights are a modeling choice.
Stretch-heavy (eccentric) exercises add up to 15%; big muscles take 10% longer, small ones 15% less.

session.feeds_weekly: vol9: no. Weekly value = undiscounted effective sets.
session.reset: Rest of >= 20 h between workouts resets the count: each day starts again at set 1 (no carryover). Justification: with weekly sets equal, spreading them over more days does not reduce growth (Schoenfeld 2019) [E], and there is no data to size a partial carryover, so none is modeled [M]. Two workouts < 20 h apart (same-day doubles) continue the count.
session.fit: Form (unchanged): credit_n = 1/(1 + (n-1)/c), so the cumulative stimulus of n sets ~ c x ln((n + c - 0.5)/(c - 0.5)), a smooth log curve. vol8d refit: c = 1.0 x the targets.json session heavy anchor (10 -> c 10, 8 -> 8, 6 -> 6, 5 -> 5; vol8 used 0.4). Fitted so that, on the weekly %, one workout scores about 5-7% below the same weekly sets split evenly over two days at typical volumes (chest 8/10/12, 8-anchor and 6-anchor muscles at 6/8; see workout-reference.json one-vs-two-vol8d). Target: small, because volume-equated frequency meta-analyses find little or no hypertrophy difference between training a muscle once vs 2+ times a week (Schoenfeld, Grgic & Krieger 2019, J Sports Sci 37(11):1286-95; Pelland et al. 2025, Sports Med, doi 10.1007/s40279-025-02344-w: frequency effect on hypertrophy compatible with negligible, marginal slope 0.32%/extra weekly session, 95% CrI -0.14 to 0.82). A small gap is kept because neither rules out a modest benefit and long single sessions add fatigue. The studies do not give a per-set curve; c is a calibration to that target, not an estimate [modeled]. vol8h refit (supersedes the vol8d c): the vol8g per-muscle curve is steeper below the minimum than the vol5 curve, so the vol8d c (1.0 x heavy anchor) gave 11-14% gaps for chest/biceps and ~3.5% for forearms. c is now set per anchor group (muscles with the same zone edges share one weekly curve), chosen on a 0.25 grid to keep the one-workout vs two-day gap closest to 7% at the group's min and sweet-low (chest group also at 10 and 12) and rounded to 0.5; every build asserts 4-10% at those points [modeled]. Small muscles with a flat curve past the minimum need a small c (forearms/obliques 1.5), big muscles a large one (chest group 20).
session.c_by_level_note: vol8i: c per level (curve fitted per level); c_groups and per_muscle[m].c are the intermediate values. Gap 4-10% asserted at every level.
session.dose_note: one workout gives a muscle more than max(1 + c, 6) effective sets, with c for the user's level (vol8i, session.c_by_level; limits below are intermediate). 1 + c is where the next set earns less than half of set 1; the floor of 6 sets is practitioner judgement, not research (it stops noise on small muscles with a small c). Limits: chest/lats/upper back/quads 21 (in practice junk_volume_session, warn at > 10 raw, comes first), biceps/triceps/hamstrings/glutes 16, side delts 12, rear delts/calves 11, all others 6 (adductors/abductors/lower back, front delts/traps/abs, forearms/obliques). vol8d was 1 + 1.0 x heavy anchor (chest 11).

evidence.summary: Shape: smooth log (Remmert 2025 PREPRINT found a linear-log per-session fit). Rate c (vol8h, per anchor group): calibrated on the vol8g curve so one workout scores 4-10% (aim ~7%) below the same sets over two days, consistent with volume-equated frequency meta-analyses (Schoenfeld 2019 J Sports Sci; Pelland 2025 Sports Med) finding little or no frequency effect on hypertrophy. Not estimated from data.

payoff.label: Modeled
payoff.note: Payoff = stimulus minus fatigue. Highest in the sweet spot; below zero means extra sets cost more recovery than they build.
formula: gate: n >= 1.00 and F > 0, else no Payoff (no colour, no dot)
k = sqrt(F / n); f = sqrt(n x F)  (= k x n)
fatigue_pct = r1(6.39 x f + 0.077 x f^2)
marginal = r2(25 x exp(-n / 4) / (k x (6.39 + 0.154 x f)))  (hidden next-set check; = d stimulus% / d fatigue% along this muscle-day's mix)
peak_n = n where marginal = 1 (bisection on [0, 40], 60 steps; r1); zero_n = n > peak_n where 100(1 - e^(-n/4)) = 6.39 k n + 0.077 (k n)^2 (bisection to 60; r1)
r1(x) = floor(10x + 0.5 + 1e-9) / 10; r2(x) = floor(100x + 0.5 + 1e-9) / 100 (half-up, also for negatives)

fatigue_scaling.choice: f = sqrt(n x F) = n x sqrt(F / n): the muscle's own fatigue per effective set enters as its square root (compression 0.5)
fatigue_scaling.rationale: Simplest option that keeps the reference class at peak 5.0 / zero 13.0 and the heaviest class at peak 4.1 / zero 10.0; full factors put heavy axial at peak 3.2 / zero 7.4 and isolation at zero 16.8. Needs only the two numbers every muscle-day already has (effective sets, own fatigue), so live boards match the presets exactly.
fatigue_scaling.design_A: n for fatigue = the muscle's OWN rating-weighted fatigue (fatigue_fresh_set_eq), not the whole-set fatigue vol13 used. See vol14-payoff-* if_whole_set_fatigue_uncompressed: glutes on a squat day go negative with the whole set.

payoff.next_set_check: marginal = d stimulus% / d fatigue% along the muscle-day's own mix (k fixed). dPayoff/dn = 25 e^(-n/4) - k (6.39 + 0.154 k n) = 0 exactly where marginal = 1, so the hidden check and the Payoff peak agree by construction (verified on every vol14-payoff case and every preset muscle-day: band green <=> n <= peak_n).
payoff.gauges: day_summary.gauges: stimulus_pct = r1(sum n x stimulus_pct / sum n), payoff_pct = r1(sum n x payoff / sum n) over muscles with n >= 1.00; fatigue_gap_pct = r1(stimulus_pct - payoff_pct). Effective-set-weighted, so a muscle with 6 sets counts 6x a muscle with 1.

topup.rule:
Preset top-up at the source (splits.json = Max-growth presets) so every preset meets the ONE weekly-minimum rule
   (r2(face-value weekly effective sets) >= volume_zones[level][m].min for every non-optional muscle). The Efficient trim (vol10b,
   unchanged: never cuts a muscle below its minimum, asserted) then regenerates splits-efficient.json in the normal rebuild.
   Fix order per short muscle: (a) +1 set on an existing tile that credits it (main mover first, then the day with the most room,
   Efficient-limit room preferred so the trim keeps it); (b) only if no (a) works: one new isolation/accessory tile (main mover = the muscle,
   most-used in the presets) on an existing day. Constraints for every step: +2 sets per day max (vs the original preset), at most 1 new tile per day,
   sets per exercise <= 5, r1(day effective sets) <= Max-growth cap (10/10/6; beginner 8/8/6) for every muscle the tile credits, no new flag of any
   kind or severity (Max-growth checker, and the Efficient checker on the re-trimmed version), no red Payoff (vol14 constants unchanged).

    Hand fixes for the remaining non-2-day misses: +1 set on an existing tile (day with room, or made room by moving another muscle's set to a same-main-muscle tile on another day), move a set between days, or swap a tile for a same-slot
    exercise (same movement_pattern, type and main muscle) that trains the short muscle more. Constraints: no new flag of any kind or severity (Max-growth checker and
    the Efficient checker on the re-trimmed version; a new 'close to hard-set cap' or 'long session' info note is allowed; no new warning), session caps and hard-set cap via those flags, no other muscle pushed below its minimum, no red Payoff,
    the re-trimmed Efficient version also meets every minimum, +2 sets/day and 1 new tile/day vs the original (pre-vol14b) preset.
(c) vol14b 1-set add-on tiles: remove and put +1 on an existing tile for that muscle if that passes; else make it 2 sets if that passes; else drop it
